title: Derived slice compatibility and pullback of section localizations
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] represented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and a ring map, and let $V\in\mathcal D$ with $U=u(V)$. Write $f_V$ for the induced morphism on localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. For every $M\in D(R_X)$ and $N\in D(R_Y)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$j_V^*Rf_*M\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*M,\qquad j_U^*Lf^*N\cong L(f_V)^*j_V^*N.$$ 
For every section $a\in R_Y(V)$, with image $a'=f^\sharp(a)\in R_X(U)$, the second comparison identifies $L(f_V)^*(R_Y|_V[1/a])$ with $R_X|_U[1/a']$. These comparisons are natural and compatible with the derived adjunction units and counits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the given site presentation. Write $\lambda^0:(f_V)^*j_V^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_U^*f^*$ and $\beta^0:j_V^*f_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_V)_*j_U^*$ for its ordinary module comparisons. The latter is the identity on $G(u(T))$ at $T\to V$, including the coefficient action. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], both restrictions are exact. Therefore termwise restriction preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms and defines the functors $j_U^*,j_V^*$ on unbounded derived categories. The sites and their slices are small in the module universe by the conventions in the statement; no bound on the complexes is needed.

source.place: Tags 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites), 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; exact restriction on complexes

proof.text: Choose a representative $A$ of $N$ and a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to A$ with $P$ K-flat and termwise flat, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Restriction $j_V^*$ is the module pullback along the localization morphism of topoi $j_V$ of [lem-weil-pbc-slice-site-localization], whose inverse image is restriction, with coefficient map the identity of $R_Y|_V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; the tensor unit [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identifies $R_Y|_V\otimes_{R_Y|_V}P|_V$ with $P|_V$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] makes $j_V^*P$ K-flat with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], the two composites $L(f_V)^*j_V^*N$ and $j_U^*Lf^*N$ are represented respectively by $(f_V)^*j_V^*P$ and $j_U^*f^*P$. Applying $\lambda^0$ termwise identifies them. Call this isomorphism $\lambda_N:L(f_V)^*j_V^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_U^*Lf^*N$; the second comparison in the statement is $\lambda_N^{-1}$.

The full subcategory of K-flat complexes with flat terms, localized at its quasi-isomorphisms, is equivalent to $D(R_Y)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. On this subcategory, $\lambda^0$ is a natural isomorphism of the two termwise composites from Step 2, and both invert quasi-isomorphisms there by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and exactness of restriction. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends $\lambda^0$ uniquely to a natural isomorphism $\lambda$. This also proves independence from the resolution $P$, with the canonical resolution comparisons of the derived-pullback node.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), canonical descent from flat K-flat representatives

proof.text: Choose a representative $B$ of $M$ and a K-injective resolution $s:B\to I$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By exactness, $j_U^*s$ is a quasi-isomorphism; by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $j_U^*I$ is K-injective. The K-injective computation theorem [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] represents $Rf_*M$ by $f_*I$ and $R(f_V)_*j_U^*M$ by $(f_V)_*j_U^*I$. Thus $\beta^0_I$ represents an isomorphism $\beta_M:j_V^*Rf_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f_V)_*j_U^*M$. Every derived map between the source objects is represented on their K-injective representatives by a homotopy class [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Restriction and the additive direct images preserve homotopies, and $\beta^0$ is natural on complexes. Hence $\beta$ is natural and independent of the representatives and resolutions.

Check the ordinary adjunction normalization before deriving. For modules $A,B$ and $h:A\to f_*B$, let $h^\flat:f^*A\to B$ be its inverse adjunct under [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Then
$$j_U^*(h^\flat)\lambda^0_A=(\beta^0_B\,j_V^*h)^\flat_V.$$
Indeed, at $W\to U$, a local inverse-image generator is represented by $T\to V$, $w:W\to u(T)$ over $U$ and $x\in A(T)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. With a scalar $r\in R_X(W)$, both maps send $r\otimes[x]$ to $r\,w^*(h_T(x))\in B(W)$. The map from the local inverse image to the restricted global one forgets $T\to V$; its ring map is the restricted structural map from Step 1. The formula respects the colimit and tensor relations and hence their sheafifications. This proves the equality for all sections. Applying it degreewise and to homotopies gives the same equation for the homotopy-category adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy].

To check the derived adjunction on every arrow $h:N\to Rf_*M$, represent $M$ by $B\xrightarrow{s}I$ as in Step 4. First the hypotheses of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] for $f^*\dashv f_*$. Ind side: for a quasi-isomorphism $s':B\to I'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $g_{s'}:I'\to I$ with $g_{s'}s'=s$ (lift $Q(s)Q(s')^{-1}$; injectivity on $\operatorname{Hom}(B,I)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(I',I)$); uniqueness gives $g_{s''}a=g_{s'}$ for every arrow $a:s'\to s''$ and $g_s=1$. Put $p_{s'}=\theta\,Q(f_*g_{s'})$, with $\theta:Q(f_*I)\cong Rf_*M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Stage $s$, section $\theta^{-1}$ and the arrows $g_{s'}:s'\to s$ satisfy [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram]. Pro side: for a quasi-isomorphism $t':P'\to A$ put $u_{t'}=\epsilon_{P'}Lf^*(Q t')^{-1}$, a cone by naturality of $\epsilon$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. For a flat K-flat stage $t_0$ the leg $u_{t_0}$ is invertible; put $r=u_{t_0}^{-1}$. Given $t'$, cofilteredness gives a stage over $t_0$ and $t'$; precomposing a flat K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a stage $m$ with $u_m$ invertible, and every transition from $m$ to $t'$ equals $u_{t'}u_m^{-1}=u_{t'}\,r\,Q f^*(m\to t_0)$, as [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] requires. Now the right-fraction representation [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation, lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], followed by a flat K-flat resolution of its denominator, writes $h=p_s Q(k)Q(t)^{-1}$ with $t:P\to A$ a quasi-isomorphism, $P$ flat K-flat, and $k:P\to f_*I$ in the homotopy category. The formula of the cited lemma gives the inverse adjunct
$$Q(s)^{-1}Q(k^\flat)\,\alpha_t,$$
with $\alpha_t=u_t:Lf^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(f^*P)$ the resolution comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. No K-flat complex is treated as K-projective and $f_*I$ is not asserted K-injective.

Restrict the fraction of Step 6. It becomes $Q(\beta^0_Ij_V^*k)Q(j_V^*t)^{-1}$ on the slice, under $\beta_M$; $j_V^*t$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $j_U^*s$ is a K-injective resolution. Apply the same pre-derived-adjunction formula on the slice; its hypotheses hold by the argument of Step 6 for $f_V$, with the K-injective $j_U^*I$ and flat K-flat stages. Step 5 identifies its middle arrow with $j_U^*(k^\flat)\lambda^0_P$, and the definition of $\lambda$ identifies its K-flat resolution comparisons with $j_U^*\alpha_t$. Thus, writing $h^\flat:Lf^*N\to M$ for the global inverse adjunct,
$$(\beta_M\,j_V^*h)^\flat_V=j_U^*(h^\flat)\lambda_N.$$
This holds for every $h$ since every $h$ has the fraction form in Step 6. Both inverse adjuncts are independent of the fraction by the cited bijection, so this equality is canonical.

proof.text:
Take $N=Rf_*M$, $h=1$ in Step 7. Its global inverse adjunct is $\varepsilon_M$, and its local inverse adjunct is $\varepsilon^V_{j_U^*M}L(f_V)^*(\beta_M)$, so
$$\varepsilon^V_{j_U^*M}L(f_V)^*(\beta_M)=j_U^*(\varepsilon_M)\lambda_{Rf_*M}.$$
Take instead $M=Lf^*N$ and $h=\eta_N$. Its inverse adjunct is $1_{Lf^*N}$ by the triangle identity. Thus the inverse adjunct of $\beta_{Lf^*N}j_V^*(\eta_N)$ is $\lambda_N$. Taking its adjunct and then applying $R(f_V)_*(\lambda_N^{-1})$ gives
$$R(f_V)_*(\lambda_N^{-1})\,\beta_{Lf^*N}\,j_V^*(\eta_N)=\eta^V_{j_V^*N}.$$
These are precisely compatibility with counits and units under the two specified comparisons; the adjunction and its triangle identities are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); elementary specialization of the adjunction-bijection equation

proof.text: Work on the target slice and abbreviate $R=R_Y|_V$, $S=R_X|_U$, $F=(f_V)^*$. The sheaf $R[1/a]$ is the colimit in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of the sequence $R\xrightarrow{a}R\xrightarrow{a}R\to\cdots$. To verify this, the colimit is the sheafification of the sectionwise colimit [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. For every slice object $T$, the map from its $n$-th stage sends $x$ to $x/a_T^n$. It is surjective onto $R(T)[1/a_T]$; two such fractions agree exactly when, after multiplication by a further power of $a_T$, their numerators agree at a common stage. These identifications commute with restriction. Sheafifying is exactly the definition [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. The same calculation gives $S[1/a']=\operatorname{colim}(S\xrightarrow{a'}S\to\cdots)$.

source.place: Section 0995 (section-derived-completion), definition of O_f before Tag 0996; explicit fraction colimit calculation

proof.text:
The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] imply that $F$ preserves the countable colimit in Step 9 (its index is the small ordered set $\mathbf N$). The tensor formula for $F$ identifies $F(R)$ with $S$: the inverse image of the regular module is the regular module of $(f_V)^{-1}R$, and $S\otimes_{(f_V)^{-1}R}(f_V)^{-1}R\to S$ is $s\otimes r\mapsto s f_V^\sharp(r)$, inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Under this identification $F(a:R\to R)$ is multiplication by $a'$, since the same formula sends $s\otimes ar$ to $a's f_V^\sharp(r)$. Applying $F$ to the colimit presentation therefore gives the canonical isomorphism
$$F(R[1/a])\cong S[1/a'].$$
It carries the stage-$n$ map from $F(R)=S$ to the map $s\mapsto s/(a')^n$.

source.place: Tag 099J (lemma-pushforward-derived-complete), assertion that pullback of O_{U,g} is O_{V,g′}; ordinary colimit calculation

proof.text: Finally $R[1/a]$ is flat as an $R$-module sheaf. For a monomorphism $H\to K$, its sections are injective, and tensoring with $R(T)[1/a_T]$ preserves injectivity by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] and the tensor/sheafification comparison [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] identify the sheafification of these maps with $H\otimes_R R[1/a]\to K\otimes_R R[1/a]$, so that map is monic. Tensor also preserves cokernels because it is a left adjoint [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], hence is exact. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], $R[1/a][0]$ is K-flat with flat terms. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] computes $L(f_V)^*(R[1/a])$ by the ordinary $F(R[1/a])$ of Step 10. This computes the local derived pullback functor occurring on the right of the second comparison; no extension of $a$ to a global section of $R_Y$ is required. Its computation agrees with the flat K-flat comparison used to define $\lambda$ whenever a restricted input is identified with this localization. All constructions respect module maps, restricted sections and the localization maps. Together with Steps 3, 4 and 8 this proves every clause.
